skill.name: codebase-analysis
skill.description: Analyze repository structure, dependencies, architecture, code quality, and technical debt through a systematic, evidence-based workflow.
skill.summary: Create a structured codebase map with quality findings, risks, and prioritized recommendations.
skill.author: AI-Vibe-Prompts

security_audit.summary: Forty-eight static alerts are Markdown formatting or harmless file and tool references, so they are false positives. Two medium findings are confirmed because the skill directs an auto-invoked agent to execute repository-defined npm scripts. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The workflow can execute repository-controlled lint and coverage scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect each package script and request explicit user approval before execution. Prefer read-only analysis when the repository is untrusted.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Identify project type** by reading `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, or framework-specific confi
- Next.js: Check for `next` in dependencies, `next.config.*`, `app/` or `pages/` directory
- Run linter if available: `npm run lint` (via Bash)
- Find test files: Use Glob for `**/*.{test,spec}.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}`
- Calculate coverage: Run `npm run test:coverage` if available
- `quality-gates` - Use analysis results to run appropriate quality checks
- `project-initialization` - Compare against templates to identify missing setup
- Framework-specific skills (`nextjs-optimization`, `react-patterns`) - Auto-invoke based on detecte

content.user_title: Analyze Your Codebase with a Structured Review
content.value_statement: Large repositories hide architecture, dependency, and quality risks. This skill produces a structured map, focused checks, and prioritized recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Maps important directories, configuration files, manifests, tests, and build outputs.
Identifies JavaScript frameworks, runtime dependencies, development tools, and package requirements.
Examines component, API, state-management, monorepo, feature, and layered organization patterns.
Checks linting, test coverage setup, TypeScript strictness, and common complexity indicators.
Produces a structured report with risk areas, prioritized recommendations, and next steps.
limitations: The methodology focuses mainly on JavaScript and TypeScript repositories.
Coverage and dependency results depend on available package scripts and local tools.
Large repositories may require targeted analysis by directory or feature.
The skill reports findings but does not implement recommended changes.

use_cases.title: Orient a New Developer
use_cases.description: Create a concise map of directories, frameworks, dependencies, tests, and conventions before the developer begins work.

use_cases.title: Plan an Architecture Change
use_cases.description: Identify current organization patterns, module relationships, and risk areas before a major refactor.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Maintenance Work
use_cases.description: Review quality signals, dependency health, test setup, and technical debt to guide the next maintenance cycle.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Repository Overview
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and summarize its project type, main directories, framework, and key dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when opening an unfamiliar project.

prompt_templates.title: Quality and Testing Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this codebase for testing, TypeScript strictness, linting, and visible technical debt. Prioritize three recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Pattern Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare frontend, API, and state-management organization across major modules. Identify inconsistent patterns and explain their maintenance impact.

prompt_templates.title: Targeted Refactor Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a pre-refactor analysis of [directory]. Trace dependencies, identify risk areas, and propose verification steps without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before a complex change in a specific subsystem.

output_examples.input: Analyze a Next.js repository before a new developer starts work.
output: Project overview: Next.js application using TypeScript and an application-directory structure.
Key areas: routes, shared components, server utilities, tests, and build configuration.
Priority: document authentication flow and add tests around server actions.

output_examples.input: Review the code quality setup and identify the largest gaps.
output: Linting is configured, but strict TypeScript checks are incomplete.
Tests cover utilities but omit major interface workflows.
Priorities: enable stricter checks, add workflow tests, and resolve recurring ignored types.

output_examples.input: Assess a feature directory before it is split into separate modules.
output_examples.output: The report maps internal dependencies, highlights shared state and API coupling, and recommends an extraction order with verification points.

best_practices: Begin with manifests and top-level directories before reading implementation details.
Analyze large repositories in focused sections and record evidence for each conclusion.
Review package scripts before running lint, coverage, audit, or dependency commands.
anti_patterns: Do not infer architecture from filenames without checking representative implementation files.
Do not run repository-defined scripts before reviewing their commands and obtaining approval.
Do not present generated metrics as measured results when required tools were unavailable.

faq.question: Which repositories work best with this skill?
faq.answer: It works best with JavaScript or TypeScript projects using common frameworks, package manifests, and conventional directory structures.

faq.question: Does the skill modify source files?
faq.answer: No. Its defined workflow analyzes files and produces recommendations without changing implementation code.

faq.question: Can it analyze a monorepo?
faq.answer: Yes. It detects common workspace layouts, then analyzes packages or applications in focused sections.

faq.question: Does it run tests and linters?
faq.answer: It may propose available lint and coverage scripts. Review repository scripts and approve execution before running them.

faq.question: Does it find dependency vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It can use package-manager audit results when tools and network access are available. Results depend on the configured registry data.

faq.question: What does the final report include?
faq.answer: The report includes project structure, technology stack, architecture patterns, quality signals, risk areas, recommendations, and next steps.
